ut_wall_mart.blurb: Wall Mart is a small crack-climbing wall in Indian Creek, in southeast Utah, set back and to the right as you walk toward Power Wall. A rock formation on its top rim resembles the head of a movie alien, which makes it easy to pick out from the road. Nearly all of its fourteen lines are trad cracks in the sandstone, with a single sport line. Grades start around 5.10 and run into the low 5.12s, with about half sitting at 5.10 and the rest split between 5.11 and 5.12. It suits climbers already comfortable on Creek-style cracks rather than newcomers.

ut_deadman_s_buttress.blurb: Deadman's Buttress is a south-facing sandstone cliff on the right side of Long Canyon, just off Potash Road near Moab. It holds fourteen trad lines of one to three pitches, of mixed quality. Grades start at 5.8, with a handful at 5.9 and the biggest group at 5.10, then a steady run of 5.11 and a few 5.12 routes. Facing south, it collects plenty of sun. Base trips are by a short, steep uphill walk from the road, and climbers have scratched route names and ratings into rocks at the foot of many lines.

ut_black_box_the.blurb: The Black Box is a chalk-covered, box-shaped boulder in the Big Bend bouldering area, along River Road outside Moab, a short stroll from the parking lot. The sandstone here is Wingate, which can break, so it needs time to dry after wet weather. Its main face points southwest and the rock can get very hot, so mornings, late evenings and winter are the better times to climb. There are fourteen problems, spread from V0 up to V9: a good number of easy and moderate lines, a cluster around V3, and a few hard ones above.

ut_shivers_boulder.blurb: Shivers Boulder is a tall boulder beside the river in the Riverside area of Little Cottonwood Canyon, near Sandy. It is known for slab problems that feel committing, along with the namesake line, Shivers. All fourteen problems are bouldering, and they start at V3 and climb to V9, with the bulk between V3 and V5 and a few hard ones on top. The river keeps it a little cooler in summer and trees add shade. A short walk from the roadside pull-out, across a bike path, brings you there.

ut_dihedrals_area.blurb: The Dihedrals Area is a section of Gate Buttress in Little Cottonwood Canyon, in the Wasatch. As the name hints, it is mostly dihedral lines, and most are single pitch with little fixed gear. Of its fourteen routes, eleven are trad and three are sport. Nearly everything is 5.9 or harder: only a few easier lines near 5.8 and below, then a core of 5.9 to 5.10 trad, with a handful at 5.11 and 5.12. Some scrambling is required to reach the base. Beckey's Wall lies just to the right.
ut_dihedrals_area.parking_note: Leave the car at the roadside pull-outs about a mile and a quarter up Little Cottonwood Canyon, the same place climbers park for the Schoolroom.
ut_dihedrals_area.approach: A climbers' trail starts just west of the parking, goes by the Gate Boulder, then switchbacks up toward the dihedrals; the last bit involves some scrambling to the base.
